objective: Implement the sim-header-v1 HTTP adapter for the supported Hyperliquid-shaped /info and /exchange subset using the shared simulator interfaces, with explicit local identity, bounded batches, stable errors, and no direct domain mutation.

assertions: SDK-shaped fixtures and external-style HTTP tests cover /info types meta, metaAndAssetCtxs, allMids, l2Book, openOrders, and clearinghouseState for only BTC, ETH, and SOL.
/exchange tests cover bounded batch limit-order placement for GTC, IOC, and ALO plus cancel, preserving request-order per-entry statuses and partial success.

User-scoped calls require a normalized 42-character lowercase 0x-prefixed hexadecimal X-Sim-User under sim-header-v1; signature-shaped fields are syntax-checked but never trusted to authenticate or select a user.
Malformed JSON, unsupported behavior, missing identity, stale oracle, overload, and domain rejection are observably distinct and no handler mutates engine state outside the command interface.
No request is forwarded to Hyperliquid and no WebSocket or oracle behavior is implemented.

deliverables: HTTP routes and request/response translation under crates/sim-server/src/http
HTTP adapter fixtures and integration tests under crates/sim-server/tests/http
risks: Hyperliquid SDK payloads can imply signature-derived identity that this local profile intentionally does not provide.
Adapters can accidentally return plausible fields whose semantics are outside the documented compatibility subset.
Unbounded bodies or batches can exhaust a public demo service.
notes: The task relies on task #2 to pre-establish sim-server dependencies and module exports; it must not edit shared manifests or sibling adapter/runtime directories.
